patches.old: Resistance to *other* stressors is actually reduced during this stage (a phenomenon Selye called **cross-resistance failure**).
patches.new: Resistance to the *original* stressor is high during this stage, but resistance to *other*, novel stressors is reduced — the organism has committed its reserves to one fight and has less left for any other.

sources.title: OpenStax, Psychology — chapter 14 summary, setting out Selye's general adaptation syndrome in its three stages
OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology §15.1 — divisions of the autonomic nervous system, covering sympathetic output and the adrenal medulla

visual.title: The curve, the axes and the appraisals
visual.alt: A plot of resistance against time through Selye's three stages, dipping below normal during alarm, rising above normal through resistance and falling away in exhaustion; a comparison of the sympathetic-adrenal-medullary axis acting in seconds with the HPA axis acting over minutes to hours; and three cards covering primary appraisal, secondary appraisal and the rule that problem-focused coping suits controllable stressors while emotion-focused coping suits uncontrollable ones.
visual.caption: Resistance dips before it rises: during alarm the defences are still being mobilised, which is why the first minutes of a crisis are the worst.
